hints: Focus on what type of carbonyl gives what type of alcohol on reduction, aldehydes and ketones behave differently here.
LiAlH4 turns aldehydes into primary alcohols but ketones into secondary alcohols, so X must be a ketone.
Recall the iodoform test needs a CH3CO group, so look for the ketone that also has a methyl group directly attached to the C=O.
walkthrough:
**Use the reduction product to find the carbonyl type**

Think of LiAlH4 as a source of hydride that adds H across the C=O bond. It is a simple pattern to learn.

$$\text{RCHO} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{RCH}_2\text{OH (primary alcohol)}$$
$$\text{RCOR'} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{RCH(OH)R' (secondary alcohol)}$$

**Conclude X is a ketone**

Since X gives a secondary alcohol, X cannot be an aldehyde. That rules out butanal and ethanal, leaving only butanone and pentan-3-one.

**Use the iodoform test to find the methyl ketone**

Alkaline $\text{I}_2(aq)$ gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate only with the group $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ (a methyl ketone) or with ethanal $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO-R} + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3\text{(yellow s)} + \text{RCOO}^- + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Check the two ketones**

Butanone is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, so it has the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group and is positive. Pentan-3-one is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, with no $\text{CH}_3$ directly on C=O, so it is negative. Therefore X is butanone.

options.A: Butanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, an aldehyde. LiAlH4 would reduce it to the primary alcohol butan-1-ol, not a secondary alcohol. It also lacks the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group so gives no iodoform precipitate.
options.B: Butanone is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, a ketone, so LiAlH4 reduces it to the secondary alcohol butan-2-ol. It is also a methyl ketone with $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$, so it gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ with alkaline $\text{I}_2$. It fits both clues.
options.C: Ethanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$. It does give a positive iodoform test because it has a $\text{CH}_3$ next to C=O, which is a common trap. However, as an aldehyde it is reduced by LiAlH4 to the primary alcohol ethanol, not a secondary alcohol.
options.D: Pentan-3-one is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, a ketone, so it correctly gives a secondary alcohol (pentan-3-ol) with LiAlH4. However, it is not a methyl ketone, there is no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group, so it gives no yellow precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2$.
